headline: MIGU reports improved pointing-and-language grounding and clarification gains on a mobile-manipulation robot
summary: The September 21 preprint introduces MIGU, which fuses a VLM-derived semantic prior with a 3D pointing likelihood and can choose between proceeding and asking a binary clarification question. On a 100-scenario instruction-grounding benchmark, the authors report 83% object-level accuracy, beating the tested baselines. In a separate real-world mobile-manipulation study, eight tasks were repeated three times: planning success is reported at 83.3% with semantic-geometric fusion, versus 45.8% for semantic-only and 41.7% for geometry-only grounding; adding clarification raises the fused condition to 91.7%. The results are paper-reported. The study does not supply independent reproduction, broad task coverage or evidence of reliability in deployment.
